newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-GERMANY LOOK TO BEAT BELFAST BOGEY TEAM.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-GERMANY LOOK TO BEAT BELFAST BOGEY TEAM.

text.p: Juergen Klinsmann travels to Belfast with a double target for Wednesday's World Cup qualifying tie against Northern Ireland.
The German skipper has not scored a goal in more than 10 hours of international football and would love to break that drought against his country's bogey team.

Following last summer's European Championship success, Germany have put together a ragged World Cup qualifying campaign, and although they finish with three home fixtures, they are not yet certain of topping group nine.
Ukraine currently lead the way with 14 points, two more than the Germans from two more games, with Portugal keeping up the pressure in third, behind only on goal difference.

Ukraine and Portugal face relatively easy-looking home fixtures against Albania and Armenia respectively, but while for some a game against Northern Ireland would fall into the same category that certainly is not the case for Germany.
Three draws and two defeats make the British side one of Germany's most troublesome opponents and they have to go back to a 5-0 success in Cologne in 1977 for their last win.
"We have a lot of respect for Northern Ireland, but I think we are now in very good shape," said Klinsmann.
Germany coach Berti Vogts has written personally to each member of his squad urging them to better things but he has absolute faith in his captain.
"Juergen feels much better since he has left Bayern," said Vogts, referring to Klinsmann's move from Munich to Italian side Sampdoria. "On the phone, he sounds a different man."
Klinsmann, who will partner Bayer Leverkusen's Ulf Kirsten in front will be able to rely on the creativity in midfield of playmaker Thomas Haessler, who missed June's stale 0-0 draw in Ukraine.

Vogts has decided against risking Borussia Dortmund defender Stefan Reuter, judging him not fit enough. His team mate, midfielder Lars Ricken, has been called up for the first time and will probably start on the bench.
Apart from Reuter's absence, there are few surprises in a team packed with experience, with German player of the year Juergen Kohler in charge at the back and Andreas Moeller running the midfield.
With a vital home match against Portugal next month Vogts would like more than the 1-1 draw his team managed in the first meeting in Nuremberg
And while they are at full strength, if a little short of match practice, their opponents have been badly hit by suspensions and injuries.

Iain Dowie and Steve Lomas are suspended but more worrying for manager Bryan Hamilton is a goalkeeping crisis, which is forcing him to look into the English second division for Aidan Davison, who plays for Grimsby in the English second division
"It's unfortunate but I have every faith in Aidan," said Hamilton.

The manager said he had huge respect for Germany but pointed out that his team were a useful side. "We're well organised, have a bit of pace about us, strength, a bit of invention and a lot of discipline," he said.
Hamilton will delay naming his team until the last moment. "We need all the help we can get and there's no point in giving them any advantage," he said.
